title: Cap. VII: Garissoles Resp. 1 — alleged confession said to overturn the corruption reading
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles's first counter: note what the respondent (Placeus) allegedly concedes. Once Placeus grants that the sin said to enter through one man is Adam's single personal sin, Garissoles claims that same grant knocks down every earlier argument meant to show that 'sin' here means only our internal original corruption rather than Adam's own act. Placeus rejects the claim. One speaker's bare yes cannot overturn another writer's many solid proofs that were framed long after that yes. If that method worked, no necessary or demonstrative proof could survive. Those proofs live in a later manuscript; their strength will show when that manuscript is set beside Doctor Garissoles's book.
pass_b_english: What does the learned man reply? "First," he says, "let the respondent's confession be noted: for while he acknowledges that that sin which is said to have entered through one man is one sin of one man, namely Adam's, by the same reason he confutes and overthrows all those arguments by which another above was striving to confirm that here by the name of sin not Adam's own sin, but only our inward and original corruption, is to be understood." Does he so confute and overthrow all those arguments? Can another's arguments — many, and strong, and long after that affirmation devised and proposed — be confuted and overthrown by one man's simple affirmation? If it is so, there is no argument so necessary and demonstrative that it cannot by that reason be most easily confuted and overthrown. But those arguments, because they belong to a later manuscript, how valid and invincible they are will then become plain when a comparison of that manuscript with Doctor Garissoles's book is instituted.
source_text: Quid reponit vir doctus? Primo, inquit, notetur respondentis confessio: Nam dum agnoscit peccatum illud, quod per unum hominem introiisse dicitur, esse unum unius hominis, nempe Adami peccatum, eadem ratione omnia illa argumenta confutat & convellit, quibus supra moliebatur alius confirmare, hic peccati nomine non ipsius Adami peccatum, sed nostram internam & originalem corruptionem tantum intelligendam esse. Ita-ne, omnia illa argumenta confutat & convellit? Possunt-ne unius simplici affirmatione, alterius argumenta & multa, & valida, & diu post illam affirmationem excogitata & proposita confutari & convelli? Si est ita, nullum est argumentum usque adeo necessarium, & demonstrativum, quod non possit ea ratione facillime confutari & convelli. Argumenta autem illa, quia sunt posterioris manuscripti, quam sint valida & invicta, tum fiet manifestum, cum instituetur manuscripti illius cum libro D. Gar. comparatio.

choices.decision: Kept printed alius (another) in Garissoles quote; not rewritten to Placeus
